items.title: How can I rename Desktops / Spaces in macOS?
items.x_text:
❓ How can I rename Desktops / Spaces in macOS?

✅ macOS does not natively support renaming Desktops/Spaces.

🎬 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3pEbuVZcba0
#COSMOS #macos

discovery.short_answer: macOS does not natively support renaming Desktops/Spaces.
discovery.full_answer: macOS does not provide a built-in way to rename Desktops or Spaces in Mission Control. However, when you put an application into fullscreen mode, the Desktop will display the application's name as the space name. For more direct renaming, third-party tools like Spaces Renamer and TotalSpaces exist. These applications allow you to rename spaces but may require disabling System Integrity Protection (SIP) partially, which has security implications. Users should carefully read about SIP before making changes. These third-party solutions may not fully support ARM-based Macs yet. Therefore, renaming Desktops/Spaces requires external software and some system modifications, as no native feature exists for this purpose.
discovery.grok_perspective: Interface limitations in system settings offer no direct controls for labeling multiple desktops. Any attempted customizations may not persist reliably across restarts or updates.

items.title: Where is the oil coming from on this cleaned bearing?
items.x_text:
❓ Where is the oil coming from on this cleaned bearing?

✅ The oil comes from inside the porous sintered bearing material.

🎬 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nu7ujtgd1nA
#COSMOS #dryer

discovery.short_answer: The oil comes from inside the porous sintered bearing material.
discovery.full_answer: Sintered bearings are made from powdered metal compressed and heated to form a porous structure. This porous metal contains tiny air spaces that are filled with oil or grease during manufacturing. When the bearing is in use, friction generates heat, causing the oil trapped inside these pores to seep out and lubricate the bearing surface. This lubrication prevents direct metal-to-metal contact and reduces wear. Even if the bearing appears clean, the oil inside the pores can still emerge, which is why oil may be seen on a cleaned bearing. Removing this oil can shorten the bearing's lifespan, as it is essential for proper lubrication.
discovery.grok_perspective: Determining the precise source of any remaining oil on a cleaned bearing is difficult from appearance alone and may depend on factors like prior use or incomplete cleaning. Additional testing would be needed for confirmation.

items.title: Where can I find a daily exchange rate from EUR to USD that the IRS accepts?
items.x_text:
❓ Where can I find a daily exchange rate from EUR to USD that the IRS accepts?

✅ Use any consistent posted rate; Federal Reserve rates are preferred.

🎬 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6O2aEdiBX_c
#COSMOS #taxes

discovery.short_answer: Use any consistent posted rate; Federal Reserve rates are preferred.
discovery.full_answer: The IRS does not have an official exchange rate for converting foreign currency to U.S. dollars. Taxpayers can use any posted exchange rate as long as it is applied consistently. For single-day transactions, use the exchange rate on that specific day. For income received evenly throughout the year, the yearly average exchange rate can be used. While any posted rate is acceptable, government-backed sources like the Federal Reserve's rates are often preferred for reliability. The key is to choose a rate that fits the facts and circumstances of your situation and apply it consistently when filing your tax return.
discovery.grok_perspective: Taxpayers should review IRS publications directly for any rate preferences, since acceptance may hinge on specific filing details and consistency rather than a single source.

items.title: How can I transfer a calculated stair stringer diagram to my lumber?
items.x_text:
❓ How can I transfer a calculated stair stringer diagram to my lumber?

✅ Use a framing square to mark rise and tread on lumber, then cut carefully.

🎬 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RTFKHkISQO8
#COSMOS #stairs

discovery.short_answer: Use a framing square to mark rise and tread on lumber, then cut carefully.
discovery.full_answer: To transfer a stair stringer diagram to lumber, start by using a framing square. Align the square's legs with the board edge, matching the step height (rise) on one leg and tread depth on the other. Trace the square's outline, then move it along the board to mark each step. Adjust the bottom and top steps for tread thickness and hanger lumber as needed. Cut the stringer carefully along the marked lines, avoiding overcuts to maintain strength. Use the first cut stringer as a template for others to ensure consistency. Check for wood defects and reinforce weak grain areas near the first step with screws to prevent cracking. This method ensures accurate layout and strong, safe stair stringers.
discovery.grok_perspective: Precise marking on lumber requires careful verification of all dimensions to prevent structural weaknesses or uneven steps in stairs. Consulting local building codes or a qualified professional is prudent before proceeding with cuts.

items.title: Strange behaviour of the tee command
items.x_text:
❓ Strange behaviour of the tee command

✅ tee prints because its stdout is the terminal, not blocked by substitution.

🎬 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NE-HYLqZmIc
#COSMOS #linux

discovery.short_answer: tee prints because its stdout is the terminal, not blocked by substitution.
discovery.full_answer: In the described scenario, Bash does not wait for command substitution to finish before returning the prompt, so the prompt appears immediately. The tee command receives input via stdin redirection, but its stdout remains connected to the terminal, which is why the output (e.g., 'text1') is printed normally. Redirecting /dev/null outside the parentheses causes echo to write to /dev/null, tee reads nothing, and no files are written. If the substitution is slowed down (e.g., with sleep), the prompt still returns instantly, and the output appears later, confirming that nothing is blocking the prompt. This behavior explains why tee outputs text even though it seems like it should be blocked or delayed.
discovery.grok_perspective: The tee behavior in the described scenario may hinge on specific shell redirection details not visible in the untrusted text. Exact reproduction would require the full command context to assess.
